newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cerj pre-tender document published.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cerj pre-tender document published.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro state has published a pre-tender document for the privatization of electricity distributor Cerj which is being sold off November 20, said a state planning department spokesman.
The pre-tender document states that any consortium interested in acquiring Cerj will have to include a power company, the spokesman said.
This power firm must have at least 1 million customers, sales of at least 5,000 gigawatts in 1995 and less than 12 percent energy losses, he added.
Cerj employees have the right to acquire 10 percent of Cerj's share capital currently held by the state of Rio de Janeiro, he said. The state holds 78 percent of Cerj's capital.
Cerj employees will be granted a 30 percent discount on the minimum price, he added.
The remaining 68 percent will be sold off in one block to a consortium during a closed envelope auction.

The pre-tender document does not include the power firm's minimum price which is due to be announced in the final tender document October 11, the spokesman said. Details on the use of privatization bonds will also be announced October 11.
The company has been valued at 700 million reais ($700 million) by the state, but the consortium led by Banco Garantia which is drawing up the privatization model for Cerj will set the final price.
Investors will probably be able to pay 30 percent of the sale price in privatization bonds and 70 percent in cash.
Consortia interested in participating in Cerj's auction will have to pre-qualify by November 4.

The power firm supplies 25 percent of Rio de Janeiro state's electricity and serves around 1.2 million customers. The company's turnover has been estimated at 600 million reais ($600 million) for this year.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
